To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed a fusion protein, CRM197(A), which contains the catalytic domain of CRM197 and the E2 protein of the Hepatitis E virus (HEV).
the non‐toxic diphtheria CRM197 fragment A can serve as an intra‐adjuvant for the non‐particulated immunogen, E2, to remarkably enhance its immunogenicity and efficacy in a preclinical model.
the fusion non‐particular protein of HEV E2 and the CRM197 fragmentA can be used for vaccine design and can improve the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of HEV E 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel hepatitis E vaccine candidate, which may be a promising candidate vaccine for the prevention of hepatitis E.
the development of a new hepatitis E vaccine.
the development of an effective hepatitis E vaccine candidate harbored by a non‐participating immunogen of E1 and E2 fused with the CRM197 fragment of the diphtheria toxoid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a fusion non‐toxic diphtheria mutant (CRM197) fragment A with E2 protein could be used as an effective vaccine candidate against hepatitis E. Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection
this study provides the first example of using the catalytic domain of CRM197 as an intra‐adjuvant to enhance the antigenicity and immunogenicity in a non‐protein‐conjugate form.
the CRM197(A) fragment A alone can be used as an intra‐ molecular adjuvant to significantly enhance the immunogenic potential of the target of concern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a novel non‐particulated vaccine candidate, which could be used for the prevention of hepatitis E. Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is the major etiological agent of acute viral hepatitis in humans.
we developed a novel non‐toxic fusion protein of the non‐particulated HEV E2 and CRM197 fragment A as a vaccine against hepatitis E.

the CRM197(A) protein alone serves as an adjuvant to markedly enhance the immunogenicities of its target in a non‐particle form, and the fusion protein, CRM197(A)-E2, is an effective vaccine candidate against HEV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CRM197(A) fragment alone serves as an adjuvant to markedly improve the immunogenicity in a non‐particle‐based form.
the non‐toxic CRM197 fragment A could be used as an intra‐cellular adjuvant for the development of non‐particulates vaccines.
the non‐toxic fragment of diphtherial toxin can act as a carrier protein and enhance immunogenicity of a poorly immunogenic protein in a non-particulate form.
